name: Five-link rear (Grzyb & Kowalski 2001 geometry)
source: A. Grzyb, M. Kowalski, 'Optimisation of five-link suspension mechanism of a vehicle solid tyres', Engineering Transactions 49(1), 47-63, 2001 (IPPT PAN). doi:10.24423/engtrans.573.2001 https://et.ippt.pan.pl/index.php/et/article/view/573. Optimized link points (p.57-58); the wheel center is the axis point B7 (the travel point of the paper), the spin axis B6 to B7. Axes: x forward (assumed; the paper does not state the sense), y toward the wheel, z up. The radius 302 mm puts the ground at z = 0 (assumed; the paper gives no radius). Masses, spring points, and rates are assumed. Library model: the geometry is the validation model in tests/data/multibody/grzyb_five_link; masses, spring and damper rates, and stops are assumed for the dynamics.

spring.note: spring points assumed (not in the source)

camber_shim.note: eccentric on the upper link 5 (assumed adjuster)
